premises.text: Guild blends social gaming with career advancement so professionals compete, connect, and advance
premises.evidence_span: Guild is where social gaming meets career advancement for technology professionals. Professionals compete on Guild, connect, and advance their careers

premises.text: Sponsored competitions include varied challenges from brain teasers to coding
premises.evidence_span: This is a brain buster, just types of things you can expect. And a second one is more of a coding question

premises.text: Profile/career center imports resumes and tracks certifications and achievements
premises.evidence_span: Here's my resume information, what you would expect on a profile. I can import it from LinkedIn or Facebook

premises.text: Skills scoring and 30+ topic certifications with portable badges
premises.evidence_span: We offer over 30 different topics and certifications. It tells me how I scored there, and I've earned a bronze badge, which I can take with me wherever I want

premises.text: Jobs are recommended with pre-apply skill feedback and post-apply ranking guidance
premises.evidence_span: it is recommending jobs that I should be applying for, where I have a good chance of getting an interview

premises.text: Hiring managers sponsor competitions and browse ranked participants to invite
premises.evidence_span: I see that almost 3,500 people came and competed in this competition

premises.text: Free for talent; charge employers; direct connection without agencies
premises.evidence_span: Guild is free for professionals. We monetize by charging employers

value.text: Professionals advance careers by competing and connecting on Guild
value.evidence_span: for professionals, Guild is a place to compete, connect, and advance their careers

causal_links.evidence_span: This is the problem Guild solves
how does Guild Help me as an employer

notes: 3500 competitors figure is competition-scale mechanism evidence kept inside employer premise rather than pure traction.
